purpose: Category-level research for the physical AI stack beyond GPUs: networking, optics, memory/HBM packaging, power reliability, cooling and industrial automation. Research-only; no site/UI/scoring changes.
categoryRead: The physical-AI thesis strengthened again through cooling. On Aug. 31 SLB agreed to acquire Kelvion for about $3.4bn cash plus $0.7bn assumed debt. The combined business is expected to exceed $2bn of 2026 data-centre revenue and ~$300m adjusted EBITDA, with SLB targeting $4.5-5.0bn revenue and $700-800m adjusted EBITDA in 2028. This is unusually useful evidence that cooling/thermal management is becoming a strategic infrastructure layer, while financing and valuation discipline still matter across AI capex.

BDC.read: Record Q2 orders and explicit AI-data-centre/physical-AI demand remain strong confirmation without requiring direct GPU valuation exposure.

GNRC.read: Roughly $1.6bn data-centre backlog remains a direct contracted expression of grid-constrained reliability demand.

AMKR.read: NVIDIA demand acceleration and its $1.5bn multi-year prepayment support packaging utilisation and financing quality; heavy capex/FCF conversion remain constraints.

0522.HK.role: HBM TCB/hybrid bonding + photonics + AI-server SMT
0522.HK.read: HBM/advanced-packaging equipment demand remains strong; qualification/order conversion and valuation remain the next tests.

SLB.read: Research-priority upgrade after the Kelvion acquisition. Purchase price is ~11x estimated 2026 EBITDA before synergies/~8.5x including expected run-rate synergies. SLB expects first-year EPS/FCF-per-share accretion, ~$120m annual EBITDA synergies within three years, and net debt/EBITDA within its <=1.5x target. Differentiated exposure, but integration and the rapid pivot from oilfield services into data-centre infrastructure require monitoring.

AGKO.read: High-priority IPO watch. Aggreko monetises time-to-power while permanent grid connections lag. Do not promote until IPO valuation, leverage and sponsor sell-down are known.

existingCoreCrossRead.GEV: Generation/grid demand remains the highest-quality structural layer.
existingCoreCrossRead.ETN: Switchgear and power management remain a core rack-to-grid bottleneck.
existingCoreCrossRead.PWR: Transmission/substations remain essential for large-load interconnection.
existingCoreCrossRead.POWL: Order/backlog evidence remains strong; valuation/execution constrain entry quality.
existingCoreCrossRead.VRT: Cooling/power-management demand is further validated by strategic M&A, but valuation discipline remains necessary.
existingCoreCrossRead.ROK: Profitable factory/warehouse automation remains the preferred first-wave robotics/physical-AI expression.

memoryPackagingInterpretation: NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 result keeps the near-term demand case intact and preserves the importance of memory availability and packaging capacity. AMKR customer-funded expansion and ASMPT HBM bonding exposure remain differentiated scarce integration steps.
powerReliabilityInterpretation: The strongest second-order AI expressions remain grid interconnection, switchgear, firm generation, backup/temporary power, cooling and water. SLB/Kelvion adds independent corporate-capital evidence that thermal management is large enough to become a strategic industrial market.
roboticsRead: No adoption-wave change: warehouse/fixed industrial automation first, cobots/mobile manipulation second, industrial humanoids third, open-world/general-purpose robots last. Chinese humanoid shipment scale is rising, but factory-job readiness remains inferior to conventional automation.
nextTests: SLB/Kelvion regulatory close, integration and 2028 target execution
